text: My favourite thing about my mum is how much she loves nature walks in the park, and how she gently inspires me to do the same without ever forcing it. She finds joy in the simplest things—the rustling of leaves, the morning breeze, the sound of birds, and the quiet rhythm of footsteps along familiar paths. When she walks, she slows down to notice everything around her, as if the world is something worth appreciating in every small detail. And somehow, just by being herself, she makes me want to slow down too, to breathe a little deeper and notice life beyond the rush of everyday routines. Walking with her doesn’t feel like exercise—it feels like spending time in calmness together. Through her love for nature, she has quietly taught me that peace doesn’t need to be found far away; sometimes it’s already right there in a simple walk at the park with someone you love.

text: My favourite thing about my mum is the way she sings Teresa Teng songs so naturally, as if the whole world becomes softer when she does. When she goes to the old folks’ home, she doesn’t just sing—she brings memories back to life for the elderly. Her voice carries those familiar melodies that many of them grew up with, and suddenly you can see their faces light up, some smiling quietly, some even humming along with her. It’s never about performing. It’s about connection. She sings with warmth, patience, and heart, gently filling the room with comfort and nostalgia. In those moments, she becomes more than just my mum—she becomes a little source of joy for people who may otherwise feel forgotten. Watching her do that makes me realise how beautiful she is, not just as a mother, but as a person who uses something as simple as song to give happiness to others.

text: Title: Disappointed with the Kaya Butter Toast – Lacking the Key Ingredient I’ve always enjoyed Ya Kun’s kaya butter toast for its rich, flavorful spread and perfect balance of sweetness and saltiness. However, my recent visit was disappointing. The toast had barely any kaya on it — just a thin smear that was almost unnoticeable. The butter was there, but without the generous kaya layer that Ya Kun is known for, the toast felt dry and lacked the signature taste. It’s frustrating when expectations aren’t met, especially from a brand that’s usually so consistent. I hope this was just a one-off mistake and not a sign of cost-cutting. I’d love to see the quality return to the standard that made Ya Kun a favourite in the first place.
